company_name: Fuyao Glass Industry Group Co., Ltd.

inputs.base_revenue_basis: FY2026E = FY2025 actual RMB45,787m x 1.0246 (9M-2026 reported revenue growth +2.46%, Q3-2026 report). FY0 is set to the current, almost-complete fiscal year so that year 1 (FY2027) is discounted one full period from an October-2026 valuation date and the forecast base lines up with the 30 Sep 2026 balance sheet. FY2026E drivers implied by the 9M actuals: EBITDA margin ~28.5% reported (~31% ex the RMB1,067m 9M FX loss), capex ~RMB5.5-6.0bn against a RMB7,730m plan, OCF ~RMB11.5bn.
inputs.share_count_basis: 2,609,744,000 A+H shares in issue, unchanged since the 2021 H-share placement; diluted EPS equals basic EPS (FY2025 AR note: no dilutive potential ordinary shares). Held flat: no SBC, no buybacks, no convertibles.
inputs.debt_basis: 30 Sep 2026 (Q3-2026 report, PRC-GAAP format): short-term borrowings 9,849 + non-current liabilities due within one year 3,710 + long-term borrowings 5,081 = 18,640 (the Metrics.csv total_debt), plus RMB1,500m debentures payable newly issued in 2026 = 20,140. Lease liabilities (~RMB450m) excluded under lease treatment (B). 'Other current liabilities' of 2,084 (up from 604) may carry ultra-short-term commercial paper; if ~1.5bn of it is SCP, net cash is ~0 rather than 1.4bn -- worth ~RMB0.5/share, immaterial.
inputs.fcf_basis: FY2025 audited: OCF 12,055.1 - capex 6,164.1 (PP&E 5,863.8 + intangibles 66.5 + land-use rights 233.7) = 5,891.0 reported FCF; less finance income 868.8 (interest received is inside OCF from FY2025, the investing-activities 'interest received' line is nil) and zero SBC = owner FCF 5,022.2. Interest paid (348.7) sits in financing and is not in OCF, so the owner FCF is an unlevered figure consistent with the EBITDA-down component build.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2018-FY2025 annual reports and H1-2026 interim: no share-based payment expense, no equity-award tax withholding (confirmed absence, EquityAwardTaxes 0 every year). SBC-zero market; house and street bases coincide.
inputs.interest_income_note: FY2025 finance income RMB868.8m (FY2024 979.2m) on ~RMB19-22bn of gross cash, much of it USD-denominated at overseas subsidiaries. Stripped from owner FCF because gross cash is added back through the net-debt bridge; the forward build starts at EBITDA so forward interest income is excluded by construction.
inputs.fx_note: Statements and flows in RMB (CNY); H-shares quoted in HKD on HKEX. Model values in CNY converted to HKD at 1 CNY = 1.1752 HKD (Yahoo HKDCNY=X 0.8509 at 2026-10-22T10:15Z, inverted). Parity check: the A-share 600660.SS closed CNY 51.95 on 2026-10-22, equivalent to HKD 61.05, against the H-share close of HKD 51.45 -- the H-share trades at a 15.7% discount to the A-share, a normal AH-premium magnitude, which confirms the direction of the rate (an inverted rate would put the A-share at HKD 44, below the H-share, which never happens for this pair). All unsuffixed per-share values are HKD; CNY twins are the *_cny fields.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-22T08:08:34Z (HKEX closing print, 16:08 HKT; regular session, not volatile)
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in CNY, the currency of the flows: China 10y CGB ~1.9% risk-free, 6.5% equity risk premium (China/HK H-share market), beta ~1.0 for a globally diversified auto supplier -> cost of equity ~8.4%; after-tax cost of debt ~2.2% on RMB bank borrowings and SCP; debt ~15% of EV (RMB20bn debt vs ~RMB114bn market cap) -> WACC ~7.5%. Rounded UP to 8.5% to recognise that the marginal H-share holder is an offshore investor pricing geopolitical/governance risk (the stock has traded at a 10-20% discount to its A-share for years). Same WACC in all three scenarios: cyclicality, pricing pressure and FX are charged in the scenario flows, not stacked in the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: (B) leases as operating cost: full IFRS-16 lease cash (FY2025 principal 169.1 + interest 16.4 = RMB185m, 0.40% of revenue) charged inside EBITDA via lease_cost_pct_path; lease liabilities (RMB524m at Dec-2025, ~450m at Sep-2026) EXCLUDED from net debt. da_pct_path is set from depreciation ex right-of-use (FY2025 depreciation 3,083 incl. ~110m ROU; 6.7% of revenue) so the lease is not charged twice.
inputs.nci_treatment: Non-controlling interests are negligible (NCI equity -RMB4.3m, NCI share of profit RMB4.5m in FY2025); flows are treated as 100% attributable and no NCI deduction is made in the bridge. Net income and equity in the Metrics.csv are owners' share.
inputs.working_capital_note: Manufacturer: receivables (~RMB12bn incl. endorsed bank-acceptance notes held at FVOCI) + inventory (RMB7.4bn) exceed payables + notes payable (~RMB6bn), so growth consumes cash. FY2023-25: EBITDA less cash tax of ~RMB30.5bn against OCF of RMB28.2bn on RMB12.6bn of revenue growth implies ~-18% capture; -15% used (the 2026 bills-to-cash settlement shift is treated as one-off).
inputs.tax_note: FY2025 cash tax paid 1,343.5 = 12.6% of EBIT; income-tax expense 1,844.9 = 16.5% of PBT (15% High-and-New-Technology Enterprise rate in China, 21% US, plus deferred withholding tax on overseas profit remittance). Cash rate ramped 14% -> 16% so the remittance withholding is eventually paid in cash.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component build, three scenarios probability-weighted (dcf-methods routing row 'operating company, non-US / cyclical' -> owner-fcf.md + owner-fcf-adaptations.md). Fuyao is the world's largest automotive glass maker (~34% global share, ~70% China OEM share), vertically integrated into float glass, with a growing aluminium-trim business (SAM/FYSAM) and plants in China, the US (Ohio) and Europe. No prior DCF: fresh build. No Analysis.json existed at build time (qualitative agent still running); the scenario axes were drawn from the FY2025 annual report, the H1-2026 interim and the Q3-2026 report. 2026 context: 9M revenue +2.5%, 9M profit before tax -16.9% entirely because of a RMB1,067m FX loss (vs a RMB481m gain in 9M-2025); ex-FX, pre-tax profit rose 1.2%. H1-2026 gross margin held and profit before tax ex-FX rose 4.8%. The share price has fallen from HKD72.5 to HKD51.45 (52-week range) on the reported profit decline and the China auto demand slowdown (purchase-tax reinstatement from Jan-2026). FX gains/losses are set to zero in every forecast year: the EBITDA paths are underlying margins. Buybacks: none; the flat share count is a convention, funded instead by a ~75% dividend payout (RMB2.1/share FY2025 plus RMB1.00 interim 2026). The interim 2026 dividend (RMB2.6bn) is payable after 30 Sep 2026 and is still inside the Sep-2026 cash balance; if the H-share has already gone ex, the net-cash anchor is ~RMB1.0/share generous.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: FY2027 base growth 6% rising to 7% then decaying to 3%. Below the equity 5y CAGR (11.7%) and far below revenue (18.1%): the FY2020-25 revenue CAGR was lifted by the post-COVID auto recovery, panoramic-roof/HUD content gains and the 2021-25 capacity cycle, while 9M-2026 growth is only +2.5% as China's purchase-tax reinstatement and RMB appreciation (translation of ~46% overseas revenue) bite. Equity CAGR is depressed by a 75% payout, so it understates earnings power.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5y CAGR 11.7% diverges >30% from revenue 18.1% and EPS 28.0%. Cause: dividends (payout rose from ~60% to ~75%; FY2025 dividends paid RMB7.0bn vs net income RMF9.3bn) and the FY2019-20 trough base for EPS. Owner-FCF 3y CAGR (31.7%) exceeds reported FCF 3y CAGR? No -- owner 31.7% vs reported 33.8%: the interest-income strip lowers both level and growth slightly as the cash pile grew; SBC is zero so there is no SBC drag.
historical_growth.notes: CAGRs computed on the owner-FCF series (reported FCF less finance income; SBC nil). Base years: FY2020 (5y) and FY2022 (3y) to FY2025. Owner FCF: FY2020 2,786.7; FY2022 2,197.4; FY2025 5,022.2. FY2020 was a COVID trough for revenue/EPS but a capex trough too, so the 5y FCF CAGR is not inflated by the base.

base.narrative: Growth recovers from the 2026 trough (+2.5%) to 6-7% in FY2027-29 as the Anhui, Fujian, Suzhou/Tianjin and US capacity added in 2024-26 fills, content per vehicle keeps rising (panoramic roofs, HUD, coated/dimmable and acoustic glass lift ASP ~5%/yr) and global share edges from ~34% toward ~38%; aluminium trim grows but stays margin-dilutive. Underlying EBITDA margin ~30-30.5% (FY2025 30.0% incl. +0.65pt FX gain; H1-2026 ~31% ex FX loss), easing to 30% as OEM annual price-downs offset scale. Capex steps down from the 2025-27 investment peak (12.5% of revenue, FY2026 plan RMB7.7bn, RMB5.1bn contracted) to a maintenance-plus-growth 8.5% against D&A of 7.5%. Cash tax ramps 14% -> 16%. Terminal: 2.5% growth, Gordon vs 15x cap on year-10 owner FCF.

bull.narrative: The 2026 pause proves to be FX and China purchase-tax timing only: 9-10% growth in FY2027-29 as smart-glass content (dimmable roofs, HUD windshields, antenna/heated glass) compounds ASP at high single digits, share gains accelerate as weaker Japanese/European competitors retrench, the US plant expansion captures tariff-driven localisation, and aluminium trim reaches scale. EBITDA margin expands to 33% on float-glass self-supply, energy and yield programmes and operating leverage. Capex stays a touch higher (9% terminal) to fund the growth. Terminal growth 3%, same 15x cap.

bear.narrative: Global light-vehicle production stays flat-to-down, China's price war pushes OEM price-downs onto suppliers, and Chinese EV makers' overseas growth is blocked by tariffs so Fuyao's export content stalls; US tariff escalation and a sustained strong RMB squeeze the ~46% overseas revenue. Growth 2-3%, EBITDA margin compresses to 26% (back to FY2022-23 levels) as soda ash/natural gas inflation and new-plant under-utilisation are not fully passed through. Capex falls faster as expansion is deferred. Cash tax 17% as more profit is earned and taxed abroad. Terminal growth 2%, 13x cap (cyclical multiple).

scenario_narratives.base: Fuyao remains the structural share-gainer in a flat global auto market: the 2026 slowdown (+2.5% revenue) reflects China purchase-tax reinstatement and RMB translation, not lost share; the FX loss that drove the reported 15% profit decline is non-operating and is set to zero going forward. Growth recovers to 6-7% in FY2027-29 on content per vehicle and new-capacity fill, fading to 3%. Underlying EBITDA margin ~30%; capex normalises from the 2025-27 peak; a 75% dividend payout returns the cash.
scenario_narratives.bull: Smart-glass content and share gains compound at 9-10% for three years, margins expand to 33% on vertical integration and operating leverage, the US and aluminium-trim bets both pay. The H-share re-rates toward the A-share.
scenario_narratives.bear: A prolonged global auto downturn plus Chinese OEM price pressure, tariffs and a strong RMB hold growth at 2-3% and compress margins to 26%; the market treats Fuyao as a cyclical auto-parts supplier on a 13x terminal multiple.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 20%: the company is exposed to a single end-market (light vehicles) that is flat globally and softening in China, to US tariff policy, and the 2026 numbers already show how quickly FX can move reported profit; none of these is a solvency risk (net cash, 20% ROE, 75% payout), so bear stays well below a distressed weighting. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs three independent things to go right at once -- high-single-digit ASP growth, 300bp of margin expansion and the aluminium-trim/US expansions earning their cost of capital. Base 55%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value Fuyao as a mature, dominant, cash-generative industrial on unlevered owner FCF: strip interest income and FX gains from the flows, charge the full lease cash, model working capital as a cash consumer on growth, let capex normalise only gradually from a real investment peak, and refuse to capitalise anything above a 15x terminal multiple. The dividend stream, not buybacks, is the cash return mechanism, so the share count is flat. Quoted in HKD, modelled in CNY; the AH discount is a market-structure fact and is not 'corrected' in the valuation.
key_risks_to_valuation: Global light-vehicle production: Fuyao's volume is tied to OEM build rates in China, the US and Europe; a cyclical downturn hits revenue and margin together.
OEM pricing pressure in China's auto price war passing through to suppliers; annual price-downs may exceed the ASP lift from content.
FX: ~46% of revenue is outside China; RMB appreciation produces both translation headwinds and the P&L FX losses seen in 2026 (RMB1.07bn in 9M).
US tariffs and trade policy on Chinese-origin components, and the economics of the US expansion.
Input costs: soda ash, natural gas, PVB; energy is ~36% of float-glass cost.
Capex overrun or under-utilisation of the 2024-27 capacity additions (Anhui, Fujian, US, aluminium trim) would delay the capex normalisation the base case assumes.
H-share governance/geopolitical discount: the valuation is in HKD at a market FX rate; offshore holders may continue to demand a discount to A-share value.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API for 3606.HK at inputs.price_as_of (HKEX regular close); 52-week range HKD 47.70-72.50. A-share parity from 600660.SS same day; FX from Yahoo HKDCNY=X.
data_sources.financials: research/3606.HK/Reports/3606.HK_Metrics.csv (FY2018-FY2025 annual, H1-2024/25/26, Q1/Q3 2024-26; CNY millions) adjudicated from the HKEX annual/interim/quarterly reports; FY2025 Annual Report (cash-flow statement, lease note 16, capex note 6.3, commitments note, segment table), H1-2026 Interim Report (FX loss, outlook), Q3-2026 Report (9M results, 30 Sep 2026 balance sheet).
data_sources.qualitative: 3606.HK_Analysis.json was not yet written when this DCF was built; scenario axes taken directly from the FY2025 annual report business plan (new aluminium-components and Anhui projects, RMB7.73bn 2026 capex plan), the H1-2026 outlook (smart/integrated glass, cockpit-system positioning) and the Q3-2026 FX bridge.
